title: An Ex Vivo Porcine Model for Hydrodynamic Testing of Experimental Aortic Valve Procedures and Novel Medical Devices
protocol: Utilize a suitable pulse duplicator for simulating cardiac output through the AV.
Set PD displacement volume to 70 mL and heart rate to 70 beats per minute (5 L/min cardiac output).
Configure 35% of the cardiac cycle in systole with a mean transvalvular pressure gradient of 100 mmHg.
Set maximum pressure gradient to 120 mmHg and minimum pressure gradient to 80 mmHg.
Use room temperature normal saline (0.9% NaCl) as the fluid medium.
Locate or create suitable fixtures for mounting the porcine AV on the PD using 3D printing or similar method.
Ensure the inner diameter of the fixture matches the diameter of the AV being studied.
Make sure the attachment length is at least 2 cm and usable width is at least 4 cm.
Use rubber O-rings as gaskets on the ends of the fixtures.
Obtain a heart specimen after cardiectomy from porcine cardiac specimens from slaughterhouse or waste tissue.
Obtain specimen after cardiectomy or perform post-mortem cardiectomy.
Transect the superior vena cava, inferior vena cava, main pulmonary artery, all pulmonary veins, and aorta at the distal aspect of the aortic arch.
Dissect the PA off the aorta with Metzenbaum scissors until ventricular tissue is visible.
Dissect and ligate both coronary arteries at their origin from the aortic sinuses using silk ties.
Transect the coronary arteries distal to the silk ties.
Incise the right ventricle between the aorta and the pulmonary artery at the base of the pulmonary valve using Metzenbaum scissors.
Beginning anteriorly, continue the incision circumferentially along the interventricular septum to remove the RV free wall.
Continue the incision posteriorly through the tricuspid valve annulus along the interatrial septum to remove all right atrial tissue.
Incise the left atrium (LA) through the right pulmonary vein ostium parallel to the aorta using Metzenbaum scissors.
Continue the incision towards the anterolateral commissure of the mitral valve, leaving at least a 3 mm cuff of atrial tissue on the aorta side.
Trim excess LA tissue, maintaining a 3 mm cuff of atrial tissue on the aorta and the MV annulus circumferentially.
Extend the incision onto the left ventricle through the anterolateral commissure of the mitral valve.
Divide chordae tendineae from the anterolateral papillary muscle to the posterior MV leaflet, preserving attachments to the anterior MV leaflet.
Continue the incision to the apex of the heart.
Trim excess LV tissue below the papillary muscles, preserving both papillary muscles.
Trim any excess lymphatic, connective, or pulmonary artery tissue off the aorta.
Incise the superior aspect of the aortic arch from the descending aorta to the left subclavian artery using Metzenbaum scissors.
Continue the incision on the superior aspect of the aortic arch from the left subclavian artery to the brachiocephalic trunk.
Insert the fixture into the LVOT under the anterior leaflet of the MV.
Wrap the LV-free wall around the fixture.
Trim excess LV tissue to maintain a tight wrap around the fixture.
Remove half of the thickness of the LV free wall starting at the interventricular septum, maintaining at least 1 cm of epicardium at the free edge to maintain the integrity of the suture line.
Trim 1 cm of tissue off the superior corner of the LV free wall wrap.
Position the fixture in the LVOT with the supporting rod attachment hole 1 cm behind the LV incision.
Fasten the anterior leaflet of the MV to the fixture using one or two 6-inch zip ties positioned between the chordae tendineae of the leaflet.
Suture the LV free wall around the fixture.
Start by suturing the cuff of LA tissue on the aorta to the MV annulus using a simple running suture with a taper point needle.
Continue the running stitch onto the LV, not tearing the LV tissue.
Measure the diameter of the AV using Hegar dilators.
Identify the neutral position of the aorta by lifting the specimen off the table by grasping the aorta.
Insert the PD fixture into the aorta, taking care to line up the rod attachment holes in the neutral position of the aorta.
Check the length of the specimen by inserting the support rods.
Secure the PD fixture to the aorta using one or two 6-inch zip ties.
Secure the LVOT around the PD fixture using one or two 8-inch zip ties.
Secure the support rods in place using screws provided with the PD set.
Place the specimen in PD and start the test.
Suture any leaks as needed.
Perform experimental procedure as previously described.
Tighten zip ties and reinforce the suture line if tissue has become desiccated during the procedure.
Place specimen in formalin 10% for 168 h (1 week) for long-term storage after fixation, wash with deionized water, and store in ethanol 70%.
